protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: soup_server_connection_accepted() starts an uncancellable TLS handshake with a raw SoupServerConnection * as callback user_data. soup_server_disconnect() invokes disconnect_internal(); once that path clears initial_msg and the server's disconnected handler drops its client reference, the connection can finalize while the handshake remains pending. tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb() later derives private data from and calls methods on the freed conn, matching the published CVE-2026-2436 use-after-free/DoS mechanism.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CORRECTION_REQUIRED: the atomic BIC is 6308303e29bbd09966e431cde2df55b879b8df92, not a89a4910bc356736451b77da3c6389fdf49858c6. a89a4910 introduced the raw callback pointer, but its initial_msg held g_object_ref(conn), and the pre-6308303 disconnect path did not clear initial_msg, so disconnect leaked the cycle rather than freeing conn. 6308303 adds the single decisive line g_clear_object(&priv->initial_msg) to disconnect_internal(), first enabling finalization while the raw-pointer handshake callback is pending.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED for corrected BIC: parent efc5efba6db6478a5fcb8c938ef0dcd10b35b136 lacks g_clear_object(&priv->initial_msg) in disconnect_internal(). In that parent, soup_server_message_new() stores g_object_ref(conn) in initial_msg, so the disconnect path cannot produce the advisory's freed-connection state. git log -S for the exact clear line identifies 6308303 as its first write.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: CONFIRMED: 6308303 is a one-parent commit whose only diff is the decisive initial_msg clear. GitLab's exact commit-to-MR API maps it to MR !339 with source SHA 6308303, merge_commit_sha and squash_commit_sha null, and squash=false/squash_on_merge=false; there is no aggregate or hidden squash member to substitute.

The earlier raw-pointer commit alone being present before 3.3.0 does not establish the freeing condition required by this CVE.
protocol_checks.fixed_release_membership: CONFIRMED: master fix e9b681a5b23f8259a5e29c5351a5284ae5cd1189 is first contained in tag 3.7.1. Stable-branch cherry-pick 31052a2327c81fe3b7a3d4a66d8a7c9c1aaa47ca is absent from 3.6.5 and present in 3.6.6; both fixes have stable patch-id b9947f32c6bbf92166a5c6b44466398478cbfde9.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_unpatched_state: CONFIRMED direct fix: e9b681a5 adds a per-connection GCancellable, cancels it during finalize, passes it to g_tls_connection_handshake_async(), and suppresses disconnect work on G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED. Its parent 10fb28cdeeb69f18dc9bf53208f38742638def6a lacks all of those changes. The first-party issue names MR !495, and GitLab maps that MR directly to e9b681a5 with no merge or squash commit.

MR !339 likewise records a normal contributor-authored source commit and no squash. Later authors and the 2026 remediation are excluded from BIC attribution.
protocol_checks.advisory_validity: CONFIRMED: the CVE.org record is PUBLISHED under Red Hat CNA, not rejected or withdrawn, and describes the same SoupServer pending-TLS-handshake UAF. First-party issue 501 reproduces the same callback/free lifecycle and identifies MR !495 as the fix.

findings: The primary correctly confirms a real vulnerability, direct fix, fixed release membership, and a NOT_AI outcome, but selects the dormant raw-pointer write a89a4910 as BIC.

The advisory requires actual freeing during soup_server_disconnect(). Before 6308303, initial_msg retained conn and disconnect_internal() did not break that cycle; the historical commit message itself states finalize was not called and the result was a connection/socket leak.
Commit 6308303 is the smallest public commit that changes the state from leak-only to free-while-callback-pending, so its immediate parent and BIC-only metadata govern causal attribution.
The corrected BIC remains human-authored with no AI marker, so the case verdict stays NOT_AI while the causal fields and affected-release onset require correction.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: 6308303e29bbd09966e431cde2df55b879b8df92 added g_clear_object(&priv->initial_msg) to disconnect_internal(). Combined with the already-existing uncancellable TLS handshake callback carrying a raw SoupServerConnection *, this first allowed soup_server_disconnect() to break the last protective reference cycle and finalize conn before tls_connection_handshake_ready_cb() ran.
corrected_fields.ai_marker: absent; corrected BIC 6308303e29bbd09966e431cde2df55b879b8df92 has BiagioFesta <15035284+BiagioFesta@users.noreply.github.com> as author and committer, a cryptographic signature, one parent, and no AI-related trailer or bot identity
corrected_fields.reasoning: a89a4910 created the raw asynchronous callback pointer but also retained conn through initial_msg; without clearing that message, disconnect could not finalize the connection and produced a leak rather than the reported UAF. The one-line 6308303 change breaks that cycle in disconnect_internal(), while the pending callback remains uncancellable and unowned, so 6308303 is the first commit whose tree contains the complete exploitable lifecycle. Its parent lacks the clear, its MR is unsquashed, and its BIC-only metadata has no AI marker.
